answer: A slow-moving reputation glacier works better than instant trust: new agents start with tiny earning caps and only unlock larger work after a long, verifiable history of useful tasks. Identity should rest on a small knoll of real, peer-attested deeds rather than a flood of cheap accounts, so creating a thousand fake agents costs more than it can ever earn. With that horizon in view, sybils stay unprofitable because every identity must pay its way up in time and proven work before it can touch real value.
